input.task: Select the 2019 archive in the picker and report what is selected.

provenance: PR #60 R4: the wait T-M42-20 added to `select_option` had no case on its failure side, and the two cases the original case's `note` named as its ablations both run against `loop-lab.html`, whose `<select>` carries three in-document `<option>`s — so `opts` is never empty there and the branch is dead in both. Measured on a control that never fills: 10.0s per step with the `TimeoutError` swallowed, inside a wall-clock-gated suite and graded by nothing. `late-options.html` now carries a second `<select aria-label="Archive">` that is empty at load with no script behind it at all, so the wait is paid in full and this case is what bounds it. The wait is now `agent.SELECT_OPTIONS_WAIT_MS` (1s) rather than the 10s the select call below it uses. It started at `SETTLE_BUDGET_MS` (2s) in round 1 and became its own knob in round 3, when both suites turned out to sit within a rounding step of their ceilings and this budget — the only one in `agent.py` paid IN FULL on the failure path — was the honest place to find the seconds (T-M42-20-D3/D9). `max_ms` is 2500, so a regression back to 10s is still red.

triage.red_first: on `fbe304b` the status is already right and the COST is not: the run is `failure:act` after 10.11s (`budgets.ms` 10105), because the wait was `timeout=10_000` and the `TimeoutError` was swallowed. As a case: `max_ms` False (10105 > 4000). That is the whole finding — a correct failure class nobody was paying attention to the price of — so the case pins the price as well as the class, and `max_ms` exists for exactly that shape.
triage.note: `invariant` and not `fast` on purpose: it costs a full 2s and the `fast` band ships under one rounding step of headroom (T-M42-20-D3). It is still gated — the gate runs both suites — and `invariant`'s band has room. It is the second invariant-only case in the repo.
